The Chetniks were Draskovic's men and members of the SDS and Jovic's men and all sorts of -- you called all Serb soldiers, you Muslims, Chetniks, whereas 95 per cent of the Serb soldiers referred to themselves as Chetniks; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So this is just arbitrary. If they say they are Chetniks they must be Seselj's men; is that your deduction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. I never entered into the details of all that, to see who the Chetniks were, who Seselj's men were. As far as I was concerned, they were all Chetniks and Seselj's men. And this goes back to the Second World War, where the Chetniks did the same in World War II is you did in this war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, a serious historian would be able to explain all that to you. I don't have the time to explain to you what the Chetniks did in World War II, and you are susceptible to Communist propaganda. But never mind, let's leave that for a moment. And now let's look at this little book that the Prosecution also has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you have five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just five minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have five minutes left. And this question, I already dealt with it yesterday -- if you want to talk about it again, fine, but this topic has already been addressed yesterday. You have five minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, the Muslims, did they arm themselves prior to the conflict in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information that they armed themselves because until the very last day, they fought to avoid a conflict and war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was there a plan for the defence of Zvornik by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A defence plan was only elaborated after Abdul Pasic [phoen] returned and the Chief of Staff of the Territorial Defence Alija Kapidzic, from the meeting on the 7th, when it was officially stated that there was no talks or negotiations, no divisions but that we had to solve -- resolve the situation through military means.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was there a conflict in the Muslim Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, why.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was there conflict in the Party of Democratic Action, the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time there were no conflicts but differences of opinion did exist a year before that in the Serb party, but there was no conflict then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was there conflict as to the way in which the Muslims should be armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of that. All that was said in the Crisis Staff was that all those people who had hunting weapons or --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, we have a quotation from Mirsad Hamdzic's book, on page 71. The Patriotic Leagues were formed in the 26th of July, 1991, in the youth library at Kula Grad, the 26th of July, 1991. We formed the Crisis Staff but the commander was not nominated. In talks, Hadzic Uzbasic [phoen] -- in the Hadzic-Uzbasic talks, Uzbasic's wing was asked to provide a commander and there was a meeting at which it was decided that Sakik Halilovic [phoen], Kibe [phoen], should be appointed commander. The organisation existed at the time, the defence plan had been elaborated, the network for supplying arms was in place, weapons were bought in Vienna and was brought in by ship where a network of the Patriotic League existed. There were black marketeers who provided weapons and sold them, and of the names who should be mentioned here, Avdija Muratovic is one who went on several occasions to Brod and Gradac to pick up the weapons and they could earn 100 German marks per barrel. They tried to get firms and companies to provide them -- with money to buy, to purchase weapons. There was a meeting with a major firm when the Chetniks started in Karakaj and Celopek and resources were sought but only Muhamed Jelkic [phoen], head of the health centre, offered money for weapons to protect the population. Similarly, we worked to pull out our young men who were in the JNA and to prevent the mobilisation of the reserve force. And on page 72, another brief quotation, despite this fact, and he is a he referring to the unity among the ranks, through the Patriotic League channels, the SDA managed in Zvornik municipality to bring in about 4.000 barrels, 4.000 pieces and at one of the municipal assembly meetings, the deputies put forward the piece of information that the Bosniaks were arming themselves, and then there was a extensive discussion about this. Do you deny that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any of that. There are a lot of untruths in that book as regards the number of pieces, weapons, the channels, and network. I know nothing about that, nor did I discuss it with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well just a minute, were there Muslims armed to the extent that they had 4.000 new rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Muslims had 4.000 new rifles as you claim, and as you also claim that the Chetniks only had about 3.000 armed persons, what would the logic be of attacking somebody with 4.000 rifles if you only had 2.000. You would be routed. There would be no logic in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well they were routed because they stood up to the leadership and we have this in Himzo Tulic's book, have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He wrote a book too. Now let's see what this Muslim author says along with all the reservations that I can make and have towards him. As an engaged author, he says who took part in the struggle for Zvornik on the Serb side with the paramilitary units, Arkan's, and Seselj's men, units of the JNA, which were made up of part of the light infantry division of the JNA of Bijeljina and under the control of Colonel Miletic; for the most part reinforced by local Serbs. And Major Jovanovic, Zoran was in command, he was from Valjevo. There was an armed battalion of the same name, Colonel Tacic and Captain Dragan Obrenovic was commander of that unit and another mobilised unit of the Mali Zvornik municipality in Loznica. They were armed to the teeth and well-equipped, and this created an armed force for attacking Zvornik, et cetera, et cetera. So that is on page 87 and this was a Muslim author, Hamdzic. He describes this and says who fought on the Serb side and he adds and says the following on page 92 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I put one more question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Last question and then it's finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what this author says who began the attack. This is according to him, and he is a Muslim author who began the attack on the 8th of April. This is on page 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Units of the JNA of the Tuzla, Novi Sad, and Uzice Corps enjoyed coordination with the Pancevo's Specials, Arkan's men, Seselj's Chetniks, and members of the White Eagles, units of the TO, of the Republic of Serbia, and the TO of the municipalities of Mali Zvornik and Loznica and paramilitary formations of the Serbian Democratic Party of the BiH of the so-called Territorial Defences of the municipality of Zvornik. Was it clear to you that throughout that whole time you were in conflict with the JNA and all the forces were under the direct command of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know under whose direct command they were, but you did say which forces participated in the attack including your forces we're discussing. You here and your ideas.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How did you know what we are discussing here? Don't lecture. I'm asking you. Did you know that all the Serbian forces were under the direct control of the JNA? That is the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, it's finished. You put the question to him and he answered quite clearly. Mr. Marcussen, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Two very brief questions, Your Honours, but before that I just wish to put on record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: -- that the accused did not, as he was supposed to, notify of us to his intention to use Mr. Tulic's book in his cross-examination. Now he has referred to this book endlessly, so I did not object. I do wish to put this on the record. VS-2000 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must respond to that. I received this book from the Prosecution under 68(1), that rule, and the Prosecution marked this book with its numbers. Every page has a number, so why would I have to inform the Prosecutor about this particular matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have discussed this for hours. The Prosecution is entitled to this, i.e., that he is informed before the cross-examination of what documents will be used. We have gone over this ground time and time again. Mr. Marcussen, put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about the meeting at the culture centre in Mali Zvornik in March 1992, and I have two questions. My first question is how long a time was there between the accused, Dr. Seselj, inside the hall and you were taken out of the hall? How long time do you estimate past there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than ten minutes, maybe five to ten minutes, just that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And how long time passed from you had been taken out of the hall until you saw Seselj come out of the hall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly that, ten minutes, not more than that, probably less by a minute or two, so it was maybe in eight minutes, not longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So the accused was present at the meeting for 20 minutes or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-2000 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly, perhaps 20 minutes past until the time I went out and then after I was taken out, some eight to ten minutes, so it was very brief. So he could not have read all of these things just off the top of his head that he had read out. He mentioned so many details, and he needed two hours to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to thank you for having come to testify at the request of the Prosecution. I wish you a safe journey home. As I mentioned a few moments ago, at 8.30 on Wednesday, we have our next witness. Two hours have been scheduled for the Prosecution and two hours for Mr. Seselj. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two administrative matters. First of all I understood ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly because the audiotape is going to stop.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I understood that you gave -- issued and order for the Prosecution to obtain material evidence about the date of the rally of the radical -- or the Chetniks in Mali Zvornik. Perhaps I hope that this should be done by Wednesday when we reconvene. That's one thing. The other thing is I received another one in a series of requests from the Prosecution that statements by deceased witnesses should be submitted under specific rules. This is the statement by Matija Boskovic under Rule 92 quater, and I absolutely oppose this because this is something that cannot be done even under Anglo-Saxon law, even under the modified form that is being used in this Tribunal, so I hope that you will not be violating procedural rules just the way so other Trial Chambers are doing. Some Chambers are doing that, some Trial Chambers by admitting these types of statements, and I don't believe that this can be done if the accused disagrees with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the second item, the -- it's on the record now. The Prosecution, for the first point, if on Wednesday morning if you can tell us that after research that you have a number of documents that would deal with this meeting allegedly held in March 1992, that would be a really good thing. You have all weekend to do your research, and on Wednesday you will tell us what you found. We will reconvene on Wednesday at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 11th day of February, 2009, at 8.30 a.m. 21 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.52 p.m.
